prompt: In Experiment 1, which of the following was the independent variable (the variable the experimenters deliberately changed)?

choices.rationale: The maximum ground motion was measured as the outcome (the dependent variable).
The earthquake being recorded was kept the same in every trial (a controlled variable).

choices.text: The color of the station buildings
choices.rationale: The color of the station buildings is not part of the procedure and plays no role in the experiment.
Correct. The distance from the epicenter was the variable the experimenters deliberately changed (the independent variable).

explanation: The procedure changes the distance from the epicenter from trial to trial and records the maximum ground motion in response, so the distance from the epicenter is the independent variable.

table.caption: Experiment 1: Seismologists compared the maximum ground motion recorded by identical seismographs at several distances from the epicenter of an earthquake. All stations stood on the same type of bedrock. Table 1 lists the results.

prompt: In Experiment 1, which of the following was the dependent variable (the variable measured as the outcome)?

choices.rationale: The color of the car is not part of the procedure and plays no role in the experiment.
Correct. The stopping distance was measured as the outcome (the dependent variable).
The car and its tires was kept the same in every trial (a controlled variable).
The speed of the car was the variable the experimenters deliberately changed (the independent variable).

explanation: The stopping distance is what the experimenters measured after setting the speed of the car, so it is the dependent variable.

stimulus.title: Speed and Stopping Distance
stimulus.text:
Experiment 1
On a closed test track, a driver brought the same car to each test speed, then braked as hard as possible when a signal light flashed. The distance from the signal to the stopping point was measured. Each speed was tested three times and the average distance recorded.
Results (the stopping distance): at 60 km/h, 41.1 m; at 80 km/h, 65.7 m; at 100 km/h, 95.6 m; at 120 km/h, 131.0 m.

prompt: In Experiment 1, which of the following is a controlled variable, kept the same in every trial?

choices.rationale: The mass of sugar was the variable the experimenters deliberately changed (the independent variable).
Correct. The mass of yeast was kept the same in every trial (a controlled variable).

choices.text: The volume of carbon dioxide produced
choices.rationale: The volume of carbon dioxide produced was measured as the outcome (the dependent variable).
The color of the balloon is not part of the procedure and plays no role in the experiment.

explanation: Only the mass of sugar was varied and only the volume of carbon dioxide produced was measured; the mass of yeast was kept the same so it could not affect the results.

table.caption: Experiment 1: Students mixed 5 g of dry yeast with 100 mL of warm water and a measured mass of sugar in a bottle. A balloon over the bottle's mouth collected the gas, and after 30 minutes the volume of carbon dioxide was measured. Table 1 lists the results.

prompt: The trial at a catalyst mass of 0 mg was most likely included in Experiment 1 in order to:

choices.text: Produce the largest possible value of the time for the reaction to finish in the experiment
choices.rationale: The 0 mg row is a baseline, not an attempt to obtain a maximum.

choices.text: Serve as a control against which the other trials could be compared
choices.rationale: Correct. A zero trial shows what happens with none of the treatment, so the effect of each nonzero amount can be judged against it.

choices.text: Check that the instrument used to measure the time for the reaction to finish was properly calibrated
choices.rationale: Nothing in the procedure uses the zero trial to calibrate an instrument.

choices.text: Determine whether the volume of hydrogen peroxide has any effect on the time for the reaction to finish
choices.rationale: The volume of hydrogen peroxide was held constant, so no trial can test its effect.

explanation: A trial with catalyst mass of zero serves as the control: it establishes the baseline value of the time for the reaction to finish against which the other trials are compared.

table.caption: Experiment 1: Students mixed 50 mL of hydrogen peroxide solution from a single bottle with a measured mass of powdered catalyst and timed how long it took for the bubbling to stop. Table 1 lists the results.

prompt: Which trial in Experiment 1 served as the control?

choices.text: The trial at the greatest sugar mass, 6 g, which received the most treatment
choices.rationale: The largest dose is a test condition, not the baseline.

choices.text: The trial that produced the greatest CO₂ volume
choices.rationale: A control is defined by its treatment (none), not by the size of its result.

choices.text: The trial at 0 g, which received none of the treatment being tested
choices.rationale: Correct. The trial with none of the treatment shows the baseline that every other trial is compared against.

choices.text: The trial at 4 g, in the middle of the tested range of sugar mass
choices.rationale: A middle value still applies the treatment; it is not a baseline.

explanation: A control receives none of the treatment: here, the trial with sugar mass of 0 g.

prompt: In Experiment 1, which of the following was the independent variable (the variable the experimenters deliberately changed)?

choices.rationale: The rate of photosynthesis was measured as the outcome (the dependent variable).
Correct. The light intensity was the variable the experimenters deliberately changed (the independent variable).
The counting time was kept the same in every trial (a controlled variable).
The brand of the lamp is not part of the procedure and plays no role in the experiment.

prompt: In Experiment 1, which of the following was the dependent variable (the variable measured as the outcome)?

choices.text: The horizontal distance the ball traveled
choices.rationale: Correct. The horizontal distance the ball traveled was measured as the outcome (the dependent variable).
The launch height was kept the same in every trial (a controlled variable).
The launch angle was the variable the experimenters deliberately changed (the independent variable).
The color of the ball is not part of the procedure and plays no role in the experiment.

explanation: The horizontal distance the ball traveled is what the experimenters measured after setting the launch angle, so it is the dependent variable.

stimulus.title: Launch Angle and Range
stimulus.text:
Experiment 1
Students used a spring launcher to fire the same ball at a set angle above the horizontal, always with the spring compressed by the same amount. They measured the horizontal distance from the launcher to the landing point. Each angle was fired three times and the average distance recorded.
Results (the horizontal distance the ball traveled): at 20°, 18.1 m; at 30°, 23.7 m; at 40°, 26.2 m; at 50°, 25.5 m.
